subject: Compact QBR + half-day roadmap/demo block — propose windows and tech handoff
messages:
From: aisha.rahman@redwood.com
To: j.ellis@orchidhealth.com, rajiv@orchidhealth.com
Cc: rafael.mendes@redwood.com, grace.oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Compact QBR + half-day roadmap/demo block — propose windows

Jordan / Rajiv —

Thanks again for the productive renewal conversation last week. To keep the momentum, I'd like to lock a compact QBR that combines: a ~90 minute roadmap review, a 60–90 minute live demo of the updated integration flows, and a 30 minute ops/contract prep block for procurement. The goal is to keep it to a half-day (3–4 hours) and make it a single coordinated session so your execs and engineers don't have multiple handoffs.

Proposed windows (PT):
- Option A: Tue May 11, 1:00–4:00 PM PT
- Option B: Wed May 12, 10:00 AM–1:00 PM PT
- Option C: Thu May 13, 12:00–3:00 PM PT

Please tell me: which window works best, who from your side must attend (execs vs. eng vs. procurement), and whether you'd prefer us to run a short dry-run one business day prior. Rafael will lead the demo and Grace will handle success/renewal items; I've copied them here for visibility. Vivek is our fallback facilitator if Rafael can't make an exec portion.

Attached: a draft agenda (Proposed_Agenda_v1.pdf) with a timeboxed run-of-show. I can update it once you confirm attendees.

Quick asks:
- Confirm preferred window (A/B/C)
- Confirm attendee list and any technical constraints (VPN, network ACLs, demo data sensitivity)
- Flag if procurement needs a separate pre-call or if they can join the final 30 minutes.

Thanks — looking forward to locking this.

— Aisha Rahman
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[aisha at redwood.com]
[Attachment: Proposed_Agenda_v1.pdf (PDF)]

From: j.ellis@orchidhealth.com

Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Compact QBR + half-day roadmap/demo block — propose windows

Thanks Aisha — appreciate the options and the clear agenda. Quick notes from our side:

- Option A or C would be preferable but we need afternoons for our execs this week. Option A (May 11, 1–4 PM PT) looks best on initial glance.
- Rajiv will be out of the office on 5/4, but available the week of the 11th.
- Procurement (copied) would prefer a separate 30-minute pre-call the week prior to confirm SLAs and PO timing — they probably won’t attend the full session.

Can you do a 15-minute dry-run the day before the QBR to validate the live demo flows? We can provide a sandbox account and a point-of-contact for network rules.

Jordan
VP, Product — Orchid Health
[j.ellis@orchidhealth.com]

Jordan — perfect, Option A it is unless you hear otherwise.

Rafael — tagging you for the demo run-of-show and any special prep (redacted keys, sample payloads, network/port expectations). I've attached our network/SLA matrix that procurement usually asks for and will send that directly to procurement as a separate packet.

Vivek — you're listed as backup facilitator for the executive section in case Rafael needs to join the technical deep-dive. Rafael will lead the demo.

Procurement — I'll follow up with a 30-minute slot the week prior (propose Tue May 4 or Wed May 5). If either works for you, I'll send a calendar invite with the SLA matrix and a short procurement checklist.

Thanks — I've drafted a short technical prep note and run-of-show:

- Demo lead: Rafael Mendes (Redwood Infra)
- Preflight (15–20 min) day before: validate sandbox credentials, network egress rules (443 outbound to our demo endpoint), and confirm sample payloads (we'll use a small synthetic dataset).
- Live demo: do not use production keys; we will use a session-limited key with masked identifiers.
- Contingency: if live inference latency spikes, we will switch to a recorded short clip for the heavy-load portion and continue the interactive Q&A.

I've uploaded the run-of-show and the preflight checklist to the shared Drive link below. Rafael will also prepare a short diagram of the demo network path for procurement.
